newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Namibian govt presents additional "drought" budget.
newsitem.headline: Namibian govt presents additional "drought" budget.

text.p: Nambia's parliament on Friday began debating an additional budget which the government said was necessary in the face of a continuing drought in the vast but sparsely-populated southern African country.

Finance Minister Nangolo Mbumba presented the Additional Appropriation Act to the National Assembly late on Thursday, reversing a June announcement by his predecessor Helmut Angula that there would be no additional budget for the current financial year.
Mbumba called it a drought budget, prepared under compelling circumstances. But the opposition immediately criticised increased public borrowing and the rising cost of debt servicing.
The revisions will raise the budget deficit to N$670 million from an original forecast in the main budget of N$549.8 million.
Introducing his mini budget, Mbumba said the revisions had been required by the devasting drought in the country and restructuring in the public service pay system.
The revised budget seeks to increase total expenditure for the financial year ending March 1997 to N$5.441 billion, a net increase of N$368 million, or about 7.3 percent.
Mbumba said the additional gross appropriation was N$785 million, but this figure would be offset by suspensions and savings worth N$417 million.

The bulk of the additional expenditure is to meet the cost of restructuring of the public service pay system, as recommended by the Wages and Salary Commission (WASCOM). A total of N$452 million is required for this, almost N$100 million more than initially budgeted.
A further N$159.5 million is to be provided for drought relief measures and a total of N$65.8 million is to be allocated to the Ministry of Finance to cover an increase in interest payments.
The rest of the additional expenditure is divided between several ministries.
However, according to Mbumba, the government can expect higher revenue from taxes, external sources and administrative fees and charges than originally budgeted for.
Mbumba said the higher budget deficit would be financed through government cash reserves and the issue of medium-term government stock and Treasury Bills.

In his statement, the financial adviser of the opposition party DTA, Hans-Eric Staby said the proposed expenditure of almost N$66 million to cover increases in interest rates showed that debt servicing was on the increase.
He also pointed out that the state debt was steadily growing and that it would have been even more difficult to meet government expenditure, were it not for the continuing effort of the taxpayers.
The exchange is continuing. The speaker has allocated three days for what he called a straightforward debate.
